audit.report: A month-end close batch job (pid 329564) held an open transaction for 4.1 seconds, blocking checkout sessions and degrading success to 53% (32/60). The Database Guardian proposed waiting three times, citing the short transaction duration and unknown replay risk, but the Continuity Guardian rejected each WAIT because business impact data (SLO, revenue) and workload metadata (registry, change calendar) were unavailable due to a federation outage. With no tradeoff data to quantify tolerated degradation, both guardians agreed to escalate to a human after 133 seconds and three rounds. No automated action was executed; the incident remained unresolved at escalation.
audit.root_cause: The month-end close batch job (batch_replayable_month_end_close) blocked checkout sessions while business federation was down, preventing guardians from accessing tradeoff data needed to decide between waiting or terminating.
lessons: Cache workload registry and change calendar data locally for batch_replayable_month_end_close so interrupt policy and replayability are known even when the business federation is unreachable.
Instrument batch_replayable_month_end_close with a transaction timeout or heartbeat so the Database Guardian can observe progress beyond 'SELECT 1' and estimate remaining duration.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian repeated the same WAIT proposal across three rounds without new evidence, while the Continuity Guardian correctly held to its invariant (I7) requiring quantified tradeoff; neither guardian wasted rounds, but the deadlock stemmed from missing federated data that neither could resolve.
follow_ups: On-call to manually assess whether to terminate pid 329564 or wait for month-end close completion, using any available runbooks.
Restore business federation connectivity and verify workload registry entries for batch_replayable_month_end_close and checkout SLOs.
Add local fallback cache for biz.workload_registry and biz.change_calendar to prevent future federation outages from stalling negotiations.
